# ci/active_workflows.txt — the CRIE "active workflow set" that CI statically validates.
#
# SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for which workflows the validator checks. The CI job and
# both local runners (run_local.ps1 / run_local.sh) invoke validate_workflows.py
# with NO path arguments, so they all read THIS file. To bring a new production
# workflow under validation, add a line below — do NOT edit ci.yml or the runners.
#
# Rules:
#   - One glob (or explicit path) per line, relative to the repo root.
#   - '#' comments and blank lines are ignored.
#   - Recursive '**' is supported.
#
# EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: the roadmap skeletons WF-002 / WF-003 / WF-004 are intentional
# placeholder stubs, not production workflows; validating them as if they were would
# raise false failures (dead nodes / no trigger path, and the placeholder executeWorkflow
# bindings they use by convention). Add them here once they become real, wired workflows.

# WF-001 Knowledge Ingestion (the one implemented master workflow)
workflows/master/WF-001*.json

# WF-005 Administration — HELD OUT, pending a decision, NOT because it is a skeleton.
# It is fully wired as of the PR-1 slice and is exactly the workflow the unresolved-binding
# guard exists to protect. But its Orphan Sweep node still carries the placeholder binding
# 'SW-016', which that guard (correctly) fails on, and the repository must not adopt an
# instance-specific workflow ID ahead of the deferred canonical-ID ADR. Add this line back
# the moment the repo-side binding form is decided — see ci/README.md.
# workflows/master/WF-005_Administration.json

# All shipped sub-workflows (WF-001 SWs + SW-016 Orphan Sweep under WF-005 SWs)
workflows/subworkflows/**/*.json
